correctness.rationale: Independent Poisson splitting/superposition shows exactly that parent-specific latent type rates B and parent-independent mark-emissions Q with row sums one generate the unthinned law iff BQ=ell A. Every nonnegative factorization UV normalizes its factor rows to such a BQ, yielding r_mark(A)=rank_+(A), with induction for all generations. For Q_ij=(i-j)^2, ordinary rank is 3 and diagonal zeros force the support subsets of any nonnegative factorization into an antichain, giving Sperner lower bound R(n). Rank<=r nonnegative factorization sets are closed in fixed dimension after probability-column normalization and boundedness, so small positive perturbations retain rank_+>=R(n). A Vandermonde HCH^T with determinant 2 delta^(k-3) guarantees ordinary rank k, every entry positive, and ell=n^-3 gives expected degree <=1+k/n^2. Independently checked exact rational ordinary ranks of Q and A on 5 n,k samples, including (3,3),(6,4),(7,5),(8,6). The antichain/closedness proofs, not these finite rank checks, establish arbitrary n,k. Caveat: parent-independent emission is essential; parent-dependent emissions permit one channel.

originality.rationale: The squared-distance nonnegative-rank lower bound, rank-three versus arbitrarily large nonnegative rank, and small-perturbation stability are established literature, not newly attributed to this finding. The asserted advance is the exact minimum latent marked-Poisson channel number as rank_+(A), resolving the stated fixed-ordinary-rank question within the specified parent-independent emission model, plus sparse strictly positive fixed-rank kernels. Stronger random-graph sampling models are expressly excluded.
residual_risks: Beasley–Laffey 2009 full text was not inspected; its squared-distance construction is explicitly prior work.
An exact nonnegative-rank to marked-Poisson equivalence might have been stated elsewhere under mixture kernel factorization terminology.
The result does not prove impossibility for parent-dependent or thinned/history-dependent sampling channels.
